Our sleek design comes with built-in plugs for EU, India, US, and UK outlets, making it perfect for globetrotters. Upgrade your travel experience with Nomad Pro, where innovation meets reliability, keeping your devices powered through every adventure.

Note — Nomad Pro shows you the real charging wattage your device is taking, not the 140W maximum the charger can provide. Every device decides how much power it needs at any moment. For example, an iPhone may pull around 17–20W when the battery is low (around 30%), but as it reaches 60%, it naturally reduces to about 9–12W to protect the battery. The charger does not force power into the device; it only supplies what the device requests. The same is true for MacBooks — a 70W MacBook will draw up to 70W when required, or less if the battery is fuller. Nomad Pro simply displays this live, so you always see accurate, real-time wattage for each device.

c2c81f17ac9e2ec371db5e5d178995c2.json.body:
The ultimate travel companion. Nomad Pro — India's first Made-in-India GaN multi-port fast charger — powers three devices simultaneously across 150+ countries with lightning-fast PD 3.1 140W max charging, featuring dual Type-C + USB-A ports. An intuitive TFT display keeps you informed of real-time power output and device status. Supports Samsung Super Fast Charging 2.0 for current Samsung devices and Samsung Super Fast Charging 3.0 for S26 Ultra.

Our sleek design comes with built-in plugs for EU, India, US, and UK outlets, making it perfect for globetrotters. With a suite of intelligent protections — Smart IC with Auto Detect, AVS (Advanced Voltage System), over-voltage, over-temperature, short-circuit, and surge safeguards — your devices are always in safe hands.

Upgrade your travel experience with Nomad Pro, where innovation meets reliability, keeping your devices powered through every adventure.

Note — Nomad Pro shows you the real charging wattage your device is taking, not the 140W maximum the charger can provide. Every device decides how much power it needs at any moment. For example, an iPhone may pull around 17–20W when the battery is low (around 30%), but as it reaches 60%, it naturally reduces to about 9–12W to protect the battery. The charger does not force power into the device; it only supplies what the device requests. The same is true for MacBooks — a 70W MacBook will draw up to 70W when required, or less if the battery is fuller.
